My father says Striga only damages after it emerges.
No. Striga causes wilting, rolling, and scorching even before it emerges above the soil, because most damage occurs underground.
So my sorghum can be affected even when I see no weed?
Yes. That is why early symptoms can be confusing. Striga damages underground before you see the weed.
What should I do?
Dig up stunted plants and check the roots for small attached Striga shoots. That confirms the damage even before emergence.

I want to store my millet harvest for months.
Dry to a maximum of 12-13% moisture content on a wet basis, and store in a well-ventilated or hermetic environment.
Is that the same for other grains?
Moisture thresholds vary by crop. Millet is 12-13%. Maize is 10-13%. Sorghum is below 12%. Check crop-specific guidance.
What about insects?
Clean the grain, inspect regularly, and use hermetic storage if you want to reduce insect damage without chemicals.
